review_text: I live in Valparaiso and visit the port area to go shopping, as there are some fantastic old fashioned shops. I also go there to socialize and I would particularly recommend Bar La Playa and the Chilean-Peruvian restaurant Taberna de Oskar, which for some reason doesn`t seem to be on Trip Advisor. This area is not dangerous, although many locals will like to tell you that it is! I couldn`t look more like a gringo, but I`ve never had any problems. If you are a visitor the normal rules apply; don`t walk around with wads of cash, your passport and credit card. Last week a German tourist lost his / her daypack in a different part of the city and the thief was lucky as it contained 8000 euros. Those of us who live here regret that this person was robbed, but what were they thinking of to be carrying around that amount of cash, visiting an isolated place alone?

review_text: Hidden away in the Casablanca Valley, the drive from Santiago was definitely worth the trip. After leaving Santiago on a hot day, we arrived at the Kingston Family Vineyards to find the valley unexpectedly cool and slightly foggy – a great surprise and perfect for walking around outside. Judith greeted us and took her time walking us through the entire winemaking process, explaining the history of the vineyard, and taking special attention to describe the extra care used in producing their signature Pinot Noir. We then moved on to the terrace to taste the wine, which was a perfect location. The terrace was set into a hillside overlooking the valley, and was very quiet. With only the sounds of birds chirping, leaves rustling, and water trickling from several fountains, it was incredibly relaxing. We were able to relax, taste the wine, and enjoy the scenery. Kingston was the opposite of your traditional, large vineyard/winery experience. We felt very welcomed, never rushed, and all of our questions were met with enthusiasm. If you find yourself in Santiago with a few hours to spare, a visit to Kingston should be on your list.

review_text: We spent 7 days in Santiago and the surrounding areas in mid-November. I had found ChilePrivateTours online and after reading the excellent reviews, I decided to contact the founder/owner Mr Thomas Proussard to "fill up" our 7 days there with programs - private tours. From the moment I first contacted Mr Proussard, to the very last day of our stay there, and even after we arrived home, I was very impressed with his great communication, always replying to my emails and/or texts quickly. He put together a fantastic 7-day-long program for us getting an unforgettable overview of Santiago and the surrounding areas (by "surrounding" I mean up to 120 km away). From exploring Santiago, to winery visits, an alpakka farm visit, Vina del Mar, Valparaiso, Andes mountain, national parks, Chilean cooking class, everything was expertly put together. During our stay there he (Thomas) was always contactable, and I noticed that he and our guides kept frequent communications regarding anything which could have affected our tours. Since we were there right after the large scale demonstrations/civil uprising took place, it was particularly important to know about these events as they were unfolding (so that we could avoid those areas). Our guides expertly dealt with unexplained complications by always having not just a "Plan B", but Plan C, D, E etc. They often emphasized that our safety was their top priority. We had Julio as our guide for 6 days and Jorge for one day. Both were excellent, highly knowledgeable guides, very friendly but professional, always punctual. If there was a 5 minute delay in their arrival because of an accident or heavy traffic, they immediately called and let us know. Even though we were there soon after the demonstrations, we never felt unsafe. In fact, because of the situation there (less tourists), everything was less crowded, no reservations were needed even at the best restaurants. Wine tasting tours felt very private since in one winery we were the only guests. In summary, I feel that we could not have had a better agency the organize these tours for us. I highly recommend them, and will certainly utilize them again when we return to Chile.

review_text: My husband is very knowledgeable about astronomy, so we opted for this instead of Space Obs which sounded like it would be more basic. We had a few uncertainties before our stargazing evening, so hopefully my notes will help clarify. We were worried that we weren't going to a dark place, because the location (according to other reviewers) is at Jorge's home. Fear not. Jorge does not live in town. We drove for at least ten minutes. He also has a lot of property (I think) and he's built a fenced-in observatory area for the tours. It's professional and plenty dark. We also wondered whether his telescopes would already be set on particular objects or if we would have to wait for him to find them. This part was actually amazing. I honestly didn't think it was possible for someone to find all of these things in the sky so quickly without some kind of help and a clock drive. But Jorge can find stuff in seconds. It's incredible. Then while the group is looking at one object, he'll be using a second telescope to find something else. One of the advantages of this approach is that he can use his BIG telescopes for just about everything. Rather than needing one telescope for each object, we could use the same huge telescope multiple times. So why only four stars. If I could break down the review, the viewing gets five stars easily. However, I think the "astronomy course" could be improved. There was a disconnect between what we learned versus what we saw. It would have been great to get information about what we were actually seeing in the sky. For instance, there was no discussion about what a nebula is or what an optical double star is. I'd love to have known, for example, why the Magellanic clouds look like clouds. I know other reviewers have said that too much information is provided. And I think he's devoted about the right amount of time to it. I just think different information should be covered. Having said all that, I would definitely love to do another tour with Jorge. Hopefully I make it back to San Pedro sometime in the future!

review_text: We got as close as we could by trekking from the Paine Grande lodge (which we accessed with the boat leaving Pudeto). It was an intense walk because of the very high winds on that day. However it was sunny and the views were stunning. I must mention that the food at the Paine Grande Lodge was more than ordinary and fairly expensive but we only stopped in for a quick bite before our hike. The trail gives you great views of Lago Grey and at a certain point you start getting nice views of the glacier. After about 3 hours of walking at a quick pace you can get the refugio grey which has a few rooms with bunks and shared bathrooms and showers. I was told by a hiker that the food was better here than at the lodge Paine Grande. I think you can also get close to the glacier by taking a boat ride on Lago Grey which leaves near hosteria Lago Grey. Well worth the trip however the glacier isn't as impressive as Perito Moreno.

review_text: The ALMA radio observatory facility conducts free tours with advance online reservation, although it is possible to get in from a waiting list the morning of the tour. The bus leaves from San Pedro and takes about 45 minutes to reach the ALMA base camp. Tours are in both Spanish and English. Our English-speaking guide gave a very informative overview of the history and mission of the facility. He also explained the science behind radio astronomy in basic enough terms for anyone to understand. We watched a brief film and were able to view some of the labs where they perform maintenance on the equipment. We also got to go into the main control room for a few minutes and ask one of the astronomers questions. Total time including the bus ride was about four hours. The only bummer about the tour was that since no antennas were undergoing maintenance, we were not able to view any in person, only on photos (the actual antenna array is at a higher altitude and is not part of the tour). We also could not see the cool yellow antenna-transporting machine called Otto as it was not at the base camp. All in all this was a very interesting and informative visit to a very unique facility. Highly recommended.

review_text: It's not a cruise ship but we didn't expect it would be. Finding the meeting point was a challenge. We had a lot of conflicting information. Finally on the day before we were to sail we received an email directing to be at the Holiday Inn Express between 9:30 a.m. and 1:00 p.m. We arrived around 11:00 and finally around 3:00 pm we were loaded on buses to the ship quite some distance from town. We had expected to be sailing on the Eden but instead were boarded on the smaller Evangelista. This meant some passengers didn't get exactly the facilities they expected. We got what we expected. Our cabin was adequate with 2 bunks and a private bathroom. The furniture was a bit beaten up and we had no key for the cabin. We learned later we could have requested a key. Our cabin was cleaned and beds made daily. Our second night was mostly on the open ocean and quite rough. The facilities on board were spartan. Food was adequate but not terribly interesting. The expectation was that all passengers were to line up to be served. Once there was no line up the service stopped. So there really wasn't much of an option to avoid the line by arriving late. The line was also slow as the servers didn't seem to be very well organized. It's not like there were any choices of entrees. There was a ban on bringing alcohol on board and none was served. It seemed most passengers had ignored this and brought their own supply for discrete consumption. For entertainment there was a naturalist on board who delivered a couple of talks but he soon fell ill for the duration of the voyage. There were a couple of TVs in the back of the dining room showing mostly Spanish language programming but few seemed interested. About 1/2 way through the voyage we anchored of Puerto Eden to unload some cargo. I was able to pick up a cellular signal while we were anchored. When we arrived in Puerto Natales the winds were extreme and we couldn't dock for approximately 3 hours. Then a shore worker fell into the water. He was not apparently injured and waded to shore on his own but we were not able to disembark because of an investigation into the incident. They did not allow the vehicles to unload and this meant the passenger exit route was blocked. Finally we were allowed to exit through a narrow twisted stairway in the stern. We only had small back packs and had no trouble but passengers with suit cases had difficulty. What makes this trip worthwhile is the scenery. It is truly spectacular. We spent most of the daylight hours on deck. Bring some reading material or other entertainment.

review_text: I used TransVIP 3 times during my stay in Chile and was happy with their service. On arrival at the airport, I made my way to the ticket counter. From memory, the trip was 7600 pesos. You are then asked to wait outside, where you get sorted into a van and wait for it to fill up. I waited about 30 minutes for this to occur. I was one of the last stops but I still felt it was a good option for solo travellers. I booked my return to the airport online and the driver was very punctual. We only picked up 3 other passengers so it only took about 30-40 minutes to get to the airport, instead of their recommended 1.5 hours. I arrived in Calama and again visited their desk. I had booked online but opted to pay in person which I found the best option because my details were already in the system but I hadn’t paid already in case something went wrong with my journey. One way ticket to San Pedro Atacama is 12000 pesos. I’d like to give a special mention to our driver Jorge who was more of a guide, giving us information about the region and stopping for a photo opportunity too!

review_text: Jorge was as awesome as the reviews I read before going said he would be. This stargazing tour starts with a mini class in astronomy - you will learn as well as view the fantastic night sky. And bring your cameras because he knows how to help you set them up to get good pics, and also to hook them up to his telescopes for a pic or two that will blow you away. He even got one for me using my iPhone pointed through a lense. Can't recommend this tour highly enough. And I also want to say that Jorge was responsive via email as I was booking, and when I made a mistake on dates - totally my fault - he went out of his way to fit me in on another night. All around fabulous! And now for some advice not just for this tour but for Atacama in general...it can be really hot in the day, but really cold...not just chilly...full on cold...at night so layer up, dress warm. I had a sweatshirt, my Boston-worthy down jacket and a scarf, and I still felt it.

review_text: We visited Chile in September this year and found Santiago Adventures through TripAdvisor after our previous agency in Santiago had completely dropped the ball. Working with Victor (make sure you send e-mail to the address listed on their website and not to any contact e-mail on TripAdvisor) was easy and we were quickly scheduled for 3 days in and around Santiago. First day was a tour of the city of Santiago, second day was a tour of a wine valley and third day was a tour of Valparaiso and Vina del Mar. Our tour guide, Chris, was FANTASTIC! We were driven in nice cars and Chris explained everything really well. The one thing to keep in mind is that since most people taking these tours are a bit older than us there is a lot of driving and not so much walking. We would have definitely preferred more time outside of the car - especially in Valparaiso. But I'm sure that could be arranged when asked for in advance. We also had Santiago Adventures book our itinerary for San Pedro de Atacama and for Patagonia (Torres del Paine National Park). Everything they picked worked well - the one advice I would give other folks is to double check (and triple check) the times on the itinerary with the local tour providers (Santiago Adventures only operates the tours in and around Santiago themselves and contracts with local providers). On 3 of our 4 tours there was something wrong with the time or location (not fun when you think you get picked up at 5am but then get a call at 4:15 that a bus is waiting for you...). I would absolutely use Santiago Adventures again if we come back to Chile - and would most definitely request Chris to be our tour guide again if he was available.

review_text: Talk about saving the best for last. This tour, led by the delightful Mauricio, was a fantastic experience from start to finish. During the hourlong drive to our first stop, he taught us so much about the country of Chile, how it was formed, and why the land is so perfect for wine growing. Mauricio was educated in Southern California (he went to community college about a mile from my office!) and his English is perfect. Throughout the tour, he revealed himself to be a total perfectionist, in a good way, about quality. Every part of the experience felt like the best the country has to offer, and we ate and drank so well we slept like logs on our red eye that night back to the United States. Our tour included several stops – the first at a roadside restaurant with phenomenal empanadas as big as our heads, which we enjoyed with a perfect red Mauricio brought as a gift. At the three wineries we visited afterward, he led our private tastings and gave us great recommendations on which wines (and olive oil) represented the best value to take home. Our lunch – a multi-course meal with huge pours of the accompanying wines – featured more amazingly fresh Chilean seafood (fun fact: the Chilean coast is as long as the United States is wide) and was the perfect meal to end our trip. This trip was pricey, but it was worth every penny for this final excursion of our honeymoon.

review_text: We had the bad idea to go there during Chilean holidays, which brings an overwhelming mass of tourists. Most campings were full and it's was hard to find a calm area, which we had hoped for going to the Siete Tazas. We wanted to do the overnight hike to el Bolsón but had to wait - with hundreds of other people - a couple of hours for the rangers to call the names of the registry (first arrived, first served). After understanding that we wouldn't be called (#120 on the list), we've also learned that it is mandatory to have a gas cooker - even if you're eating cold. The entire place seemed nice but I can't tell if it's always crowed like this. Before going, you should get information from local people in Santiago.

review_text: We spent 3 days with the Chile Off-Track girls and each experience was really great. The bright, bubbly and friendly Tessa was our fun guide and interpreter for 2 days. The first day we walked around Santiago for the day - wandering the streets, visiting the markets and having lunch in a great little restaurant. Our second day was a lovely 3-hour ride in the foothills of the Andes, a very relaxed and easy trail through paddocks of cows with an entourage of farm dogs to accompany riders. On our third day we headed down to Valparaiso on the coast. What a great city! The hills full of winding streets and steep steps, covered in amazingly beautiful graffiti, was a delight to wander around. Stopping for coffee and lunch with fabulous views over the port city down to the ocean was just great. A visit to Pablo Neruda's house, now museum, was a great part of the day for a glimpse into the history and bohemian nature of the place. Suzanne and Tessa were great company and the tours were interesting and well organised. Big thumbs up!

review_text: We had a short day in port and decided to go horseback riding at Ecoturismo La Pancha. Ricky met us at the port and he and his grandfather drove us to their beautiful property. We arrived at their home where they had a sort of outdoor dining building for us to hang out in - that his father had built. The home and property were amazing: goats, cats, dogs, a turkey, and horses are kept there and it is nestled right on gorgeous creeks. His family was so friendly and wonderful and accommodating. Ricky's brother Ivan takes care of and readies the horses for the riders. Ricky took us all around the property and was so passionate about the history of the area. He took us to a viewing point where we let the horses rest and walked up to a small field. We hung out and he made us mate that we shared together with cookies and talked about the beautiful region, the culture, he answered our questions and told stories. It was so amazing and relaxing and gorgeous! Ricky is friendly, funny, and knowledgeable. Afterward we headed back and his mother made us coffee while we relaxed under their patio and played with their kittens. Their 2 awesome dogs followed us the whole day. On the way back to the boat, with our limited time Ricky and his grandpa were nice enough to give us a short tour of town and walk around a little bit. We could have spent all day out with Ricky riding around and admiring the magnificent landscape. If youre the type that doesnt want to give your cruise line an exorbitant amount of money to be herded like cattle onto a bus with 100 people - go with Ricky. Have an intimate and relaxing day of beauty courtesy of a hard working and super friendly family! If I'm ever back in Aisen I will be visiting them again! Thank you very much for your story and description of your day with us. We are really happy to have been generated with a pleasant experience and have taken a nice memory of our home. review_text: In early March, 2023, we visited Torres del Paine National Park and it is an absolutely amazing landscape and natural beauty. As we hoped to see sunrise of the Towers of Paine, we stayed at hotel Refugio Chileno for one night. It took about 2-hour hiking from the parking place to the hotel. It was a cold and raining day. Next day at 4 am, we started the 4-mile hiking to Towers of Paine. This was a hard hiking and took almost 2 hours to reach. Fortunately we had a sunny morning and captured the beautiful and magical views of Towers of Paine in the morning glows. Truly breathtaking. At 8 am, it started to rain and the Towers of Paine was covered by cloud. So whether you can see the beauty of Powers of Paine really depends on the weather. Anyway this is a place one should visit.

review_text: First, I'd like to give credit where it's due - our tour guide was AMAZING at his job and excellently balanced switching between English and Portuguese with incredibly detailed information. There were some really beautiful picture points in between the heavily vandalized town, and the boat tour captain was also a pleasure and so kind to our four year old. That being said, many aspects of this trip were (I feel) seriously flawed. It began with an hour of hotel pickups, which added considerably to the time spent in vehicle and we didn't leave Santiago until around 8:20 (nearly 2.5 hours by the time we arrived in Viña del Mal- and we weren't even the first pickup), and ended with a 4-hour drive home... But I'll go that later. The worst offense was lunch, where we were recommended a restaurant, told it was not required, but highly suggested especially since they had reservations for the group- and that we had about 75 minutes allotted for the meal. Not only were the price incredibly high for Chile, but it took a full 90 minutes just to be served. Our "appetizer" ceviche came out warm with cold soggy potato chips, while our meals appeared at the same time- both bland and lukewarm. The guide was incredibly gracious in offering to give us extra time to eat, although it was mostly unneeded as we left most of the food untouched. It was a total waste of our time in Viña del Mar. In the end, between massive hotel pickups, lunch debacle, and time needed for a bilingual tour- I believe we were roughly 90 minutes behind schedule, and didn't leave Valparaíso until after 5PM- which then compounded by hitting traffic jams on the way home. I am assuming this was unusual, and possibly a result of our late every into the Santiago area, in addition to other accidents on the highway. All-in-all, our "9-hour" 8AM-5PM tour lasted from 7:20AM until we were dropped off at 7:55PM- NEARLY 4 HOURS LONGER THAN ADVERTISED, WITH OVER 6 HOURS IN THE VEHICLE. We booked a tour to save us time and hassle, in the end, we would have been better off going on our own. Review of: Full Day Guided Tour Viña del Mar and Valparaíso from Santiago

review_text: I booked this tour last-minute during a trip to Puerto Natales and I had such an incredible experience. I do agree with a previous reviewer that the tour is a little better suited for Spanish speakers, but I don't think you miss out on too much if you don't know Spanish, just a few jokes and some more detailed specifics about certain parts of the park. While the natural features of Torres del Paine are amazing, this tour is also great for wildlife spotting. We saw Andean condors, a rhea, so many guanacos, and even a puma, which is apparently pretty rare. If you're heading to Puerto Natales and only have one day to explore Torres del Paine, I definitely recommend this tour! review_text: I wish I could give this a higher rating but I have to be honest to fellow Tripadvisor users. Here is why; The Good: Communication during the reservation process was very well-handled. Emanuel responded to my emails in time and professionally. The payment process through PayPal was very efficient. Our guide, Hector, was very enthusiastic and authentic. At times he looked like an amateur (a plus) with his story telling but he was a professional through and through. The pick up from the hotel was right on time. The van was very clean and had high ceilings affording everybody a lot of room. There were 12 of us and everybody fit comfortably. The driver was safe, he didn't take any unnecessary risks. The Bad; The itinerary was weak. We spent way too much time on the way to Valparaiso during a break when we had a chance to see three Llamas, which were basically grazing. We had free chi chi but that wasn't worth 45 minutes on a tight schedule. We only did two Cerros in Valparaiso and those we did very fast. This is a place where you want to take a lot of pictures, stop and feel the air but there was no time. I couldn't even stop for a look at the tourist knick-knacks. They should have given us at least one free hour. There were beautiful cafes and places to hang out and I could not even spend a minute there. The wine tasting was very short, very commercial and -in this format- very unnecessary. A more proper wine tasting experience would be good though. Hector tried to get back to Santiago fast, saying that we should hit the town before the evening rush. This should've been planned in the beginning, there were still plenty of sunlight remaining in the day when they dropped us at our hotels. The restaurant they took us is on a Cerro with nothing interesting in it. If it were in one of the two we first toured it would have given us an alternative to look for a different place or even prefer a walk on our own; an empanada would have done it for me. The restaurant had good views but the prices were inflated. I had a feeling Stamps gets a cut off the bill but I don't want to blame anybody unfairly; this is just my gut speaking. I had the paella, which was dry and my table neighbor had the tuna steak, which he said was also dry. The service was good, bathrooms were clean but the fact that I felt like i was forced to have lunch there really bothered me. Among all the items of the day, we spent the most time in the restaurant and that is unacceptable. The Ugly; We didn't even get to see Neruda's house in Valparaiso. Llamas for 45 minutes anyone??? The Conclusion: This company seems to have the right people and the infrastructure to do a better job. They should put more value in the product. Review of: Valparaiso Port and Vina del Mar Full-Day Tour from Santiago

review_text: I did the afternoon tour, which in the current schedule is about parks and politics. Our wonderful guide was Stefano, whose enthusiasm in showing his city to tourists is matched only by his knowledge of all its corners. In the first part of the tour we explored three main parks in the center of Santiago and we learnt how their history of initial glory, fall into deep decay during the 17 long years of military dictatorship that forbade all forms of congregation in public places, and rebirth through ad-hoc interventions after the return of democracy, reflects the history of the whole nation. In the second part of the tour, we went to the GAM cultural center (GAM stands for Gabriela Mistral, the Chilean Nobel laureate poet and humanist who did so much to develop a modern educational system throughout the whole country) and La Moneda Palace, two buildings whose alternating fortunes are so inextricably tied to both Salvador Allende and Augusto Pinochet, that were the perfect settings for Stefano to re-evoke for us the troubled last 50 years of Chilean history, a country that reconquered democracy after being forcefully plunged into a darkness that lasted almost two decades and took many of its citizens' lives with it. A not yet perfect democracy, which still leaves the younger generations with many unfulfilled requests, but which will improve as it gets older and further removes its residual links to those dark years. All in all a must-do tour for those interested in learning how cities are living entities shaped by their history.

review_text: Nice to stop by while on the way to or from Morro de Arica (a great hilltop with a big Chilean flag, an informative military museum about the 1880's War of the Pacific & a fairly-sizeable Christ statue) is this lovely cathedral in "white & brown" (for both inside & outside) although there's really not much to see inside except a few statues, some small "carving scenes" depicting the Crucifixion (on the walls) & two body replicas of Christ (one on the crucifix at the altar & one inside a glass case). And just as pleasant to see this lovely cathedral is also to walk through the square or the square-like area in front (which was really very clean & with a big beautiful Christmas tree at the time around Christmas when I visited) all the way to the far side where there's an old locomotive engine on display and where on one side of the square (to your right) is the well-kept building which is the old Bolivian train station. And also "pretty vibrant" is the vicinity of this cathedral with a "quite-spread-out" shopping area of a number of streets lined with shops where you can find all miscellaneous items including some nice souvenirs (just a short walk to the right after coming out of the Cathedral) and also with an area right on the waterfront where you can see pelicans & sea lions in their "natural habitat" (across the square in front of the Cathedral followed by a walk of one block to the right alongside the old Bolivian train station after which across the street to the left is the big entrance to the Port of Arica but enter through the small pedestrian way to the right which will take you straight to that waterfront area for an "awesome sight" of those creatures).

review_text: We were supposed to be attempting Osorno but the park closed the summit before our arrival so we climbed Calbuco instead. It was a fun challenge and Jose was the perfect guide and we enjoyed his company. Although the first part of the climb is not dangerous, it is physically taxing as you are trekking on scree and every step up slides about a half step back. Luckily, there had been some snow the day before our climb so closer to the summit it was easier to climb at that angle. It definitely got my heart rate up a little in certain parts where you are climbing over boulders with a steep drop to either side and the final rock climb to the summit. The summit was truly breathtaking and we had a great view of the recent crater created by the 2015 eruption. I would highly recommend Jose or anyone on his team if you are looking for an adventure with a highly skilled guide.

review_text: Magdalena Island is a small island in the Strait of Magellan in Chile. It was declared a national monument – Los Pingüinos Natural Monument. The island is home to the largest penguin colonies of south Chile, with an estimated 60,000 breeding pairs of the Magellanic penguin. The islands are completely uninhabited by humans (except for the park rangers) and every summer, thousands of tourists travel to the monument to see the penguins. Our guided tour included a one hour walk along the walkway. If any penguins wander onto the walkway, we all have to stop and let them go. Penguins get the right of way! We saw so many penguins up close, it was insane! We learned that a penguin pair will have two eggs every season. If you see two chicks with a parent, it means a 100% success rate! There are also a ton of other birds on the island as well – we saw some seagulls and seagull chicks!

Alejandra, the daughter of the founder of Quintessance showed us all through the facilities where the fiber is processed and woven —- anyone interested in older, elaborate machinery will be blown away. Being German Shepherd fans, we also really enjoyed visits with the K9 members of the family. Then we got to take our time browsing and purchasing in the boutique. The second part of the day took us to the Pacific Coast; viewing the Humboldt penguin colony on their own little island that is off-limits to people. We then enjoyed a relaxing lunch of traditional empanadas from a second floor outdoor dining spot with a view of the ocean and town. review_text: This was the strangest and most confusing/frustrating tour we have ever taken (and we've taken plenty of tours through Viator and TripAdvisor) except for seeing the penguins. The penguins were amazing and after getting on the boat it was cool. Except there was no ride back to the station as mentioned (but it's fine because it's like a 15 minute walk so the bus to the port was unnecessary anyway.) It was all just confusing and frustrating getting there and no one seemed to know anything--not even the bus driver. Read on for explanation: So first off, we didn't receive any information regarding the pick up situation other than the place and time to meet. We didn't know what kind of vehicle/bus we would be taking to the port to see the penguins, names of tour guides, what the bus looked like, nothing. And even after finally calling on the day of, it didn't seem like the person on the other end of the phone did either, which was concerning. We just knew to be at this bus station where there are several buses that run, but we figured that the bus would be obvious when it appeared at the agreed upon time and place. It wasn't. Two big buses did arrive, but it was from the generic bus company (almost seemed like a public bus). It didn't seem like a bus for the tour, so we almost didn't go on it. There was also no one from the tour company to announce that people with Tangol Tours should take this bus to get there. The bus drivers didn't even know the name(s) of the tour company. They just said if you're going to see penguins with any company get on this bus... It was chaos and everyone was confused, but got on the bus and hoped for the best. The bus ride was literally just for a few blocks. We literally could have walked and gotten to the port in maybe 15 minutes, so the bus was an unnecessary mess. Once we arrived there were tour guides that seemed flustered and confused. But we were all ushered to get on the boats to the island (Regardless of company). Again very confusing. It seems like maybe Tangol is a third party for the boat company that takes you to the island? Not sure, but it seems very pointless. Essentially, you just need a ticket to get on the boat and there you will find the tour guides that talks about the penguins and takes you to see them. Up until then it's just chaos and confusion. BUT! We did see penguins and they were spectacular and you get to see the babies pretty close (of course no touching them). So 5 stars for penguins 2 or maybe even 1 star for this tour company, and 3 or 4 stars for the tour guide on the boat. If you read all of this, I congratulate you haha. review_text: Salar de Uyuni is a great experience and I would particularly recommend WWT. Like most people I'd read the horror stories and was a little apprehensive about the experience. However, I was pleasantly surprised with the driver, the accommodation and the food. I took the trip from San Pedro de Atacama to Uyuni and I was happy with doing it this way around as having the sunrise on the salt flats on the last morning was a particularly memorable moment. The driver Jonny (not sure about spelling) drove safely throughout the trip and as far as I am aware he wasn't drunk. The car seemed to be in good condition and we had no problems with it. It can feel a little cramped in the car but all companies use a similar car and it helps that you stop often to check out the scenery. It's a budget trip so luxury food wasn't to be expected. But I was happy to receive fruit and vegetables as part of every meal. The vegetarian option for each meal was an egg, but thankfully it was prepared different ways to offer at least some variety. Additional snacks weren't really necessary as the portions were plentiful. Again accommodation is basic but I've definitely stayed in much worse places. Beds were comfy and it wasn't as cold as I had expected - on the first night there was the option to have a sleeping bag. The accommodation was clean and there were even hot showers on the second night (we had ours for free but apparently other groups needed to pay). All in all I was happy with the experience I had and would recommend WWT to anyone else taking the trip!

review_text: On my first day in Santiago, I took the subway to Plaza de Armas and saw a guy in the Turistik jacket advertising tours. I went to the office and signed and got my wrist band and then headed to the stop to get on the bus. You get some headphones so you can listen to the recorded information about each stop along the way. It takes a full two hours of riding on the bus to get back to where you started. If you're going to sign up for the hop on / hop off tour, I would recommend that you start your day early so you can take full advantage of the day. I also would probably recommend that you map out where you want to go in advance so you know what stops to get off at and what is nearby. You don't necessarily need to go to all of the stops if you know what you're doing. Uber is quick and easy, so you shouldn't feel like you need to keep riding until you end up where you started. Turistik also has day trip tours which I think are probably a smarter investment of money since it's not so easy to do those things yourself. Thank you very much for your comment. Carola, the owner is very easy to communicate and work with. review_text: Good morning! I would like to share my evaluations about the tours I took through the agency. The first panoramic tour was as expected. Everything went well, we had no problems and the guide Coqueiro was a fun guide who provided entertainment for the tour. Regarding the love and pasta tour, everything also went well, a very fun dinner that went as expected. However, I would like to point out that the second tour, which was Wine day Conchagua premium 2, had several problems. Initially, I would like to point out that my boyfriend and I enjoyed the receptiveness of the guide Venâncio, who was extremely friendly and nice to both of us, introduced us to the city very well, was a very fun person and was part of the fun we had on the way to the tour, so I want to emphasize that our problem has nothing to do with the guide, on the contrary, he helped to make this tour more exciting and cool. So we would like to rate him (Venâncio) with a rating of 10 for all the support we had during the tour, as we loved his receptiveness and all the attention he gave us. However, we are extremely disappointed with our tour. First of all, when this request was given to us, it was reported that it would be all day, as there were two premium wineries, one would be in the morning for lunch break and the other in the afternoon, which we didn't have. I don't know who sets up the route to be followed during the day but it was terrible, as we had the Montes tour at 13:00, lunch at 14:30 and the Clos tour at 16:30, which is extremely absurd and a disrespect towards us who were expecting a premium experience, since we didn't have time for anything. We really enjoyed the montes tour because of the professional who was accompanying us, but we didn't have time to taste the wines, as the tour was carried out in a rush due to lunch time, we weren't able to finish our experience of drinking the wines. wines and not even buying wines at the Montes store as we had prepared. As for the lunch part, it was something absurd, we had a little less than 1 hour to have a 3-course lunch with 2 glasses of wine, the place was incredible, the food was good but it's an environment for you to enjoy the moment, enjoy things and relax, which we didn't have, as we needed to eat hurriedly and very quickly due to our schedules. We had to leave half of the dessert and the second glass of wine as well, as we weren't going to drink it quickly. We had created a lot of expectations for this moment as it was handpicked to be the day of our anniversary celebration. It was a disappointment not to have time to enjoy the restaurant and everything that moment offers. However, even with a busy lunch, we arrived late at the Clos Apalta tour, which was also a disappointment, as we had a very quick tour of a few minutes, where the Clos guide went through all the places very quickly, making it impossible to take photos and not even appreciate the link, since we saw everything very quickly and without explanation, when it came to tasting the wines we had about 5 minutes at that time, so it wasn't a tasting at all. It is worth remembering that we paid an extra amount just a few days before to be in the tour of this winery. So, the amount we paid for this tour, which was not cheap at all, does not match the experiences we had there, due to the lack of organization and time planning in each place. We weren't able to enjoy the true experience that we paid for and expected to have, which is a shame, as we selected something that was much more valuable than the rest of the tours. It is not good to do a tour at this level, in extraordinary wineries in a rushed and quick way. We took the day to enjoy everything in these places, which left us frustrated. I don't know if you can do anything for both of us regarding the frustrating experience we had related to this time management, but I would like to say that for other people's future trips, you don't make the same mistake, as there will be more people frustrated with this dynamic. Apart from this incident with the organization of the schedules, we really liked the agency, everything went well with the tours and the service is excellent and with great guides! Thank you very much Bom dia Everson! Agradecemos muito pelo seu feedback detalhado e por compartilhar sua experiência conosco. review_text: Our tour began with being picked up from our hotel by Sean (he was early so it was great that we didn’t have to wait), we started driving out towards the coast, once there we stopped by at Concon coastline were we were able to take some pictures and see some sea lions, we did not stop by in any place in Viña Del Mar, we only drove by the coastline (so if you are looking for a tour to stop by Reñaca or Villa Del Mar and walk around those two places this is not the one). We drove straight to Valparaiso, when we arrived we went to the port for a boat ride. The boat ride was really nice, it lasted about 20 minutes or so. Afterwards we met with Jen who we did a city tour of Valparaiso with, we went up the Reina Victoria elevator, walked around some of the streets (we did not go into any museums) and were able to take a lot of pictures. After walking around we had lunch at Café Turri where the view, food and wine was excellent! The last stop of our tour was suppose to be a light house but since we took long at the restaurant because we wanted to have a second bottle of wine we told Sean we did not have to do that part of the tour so instead he took us to Casablanca Winery, which was so cool because it was the vineyard from where the wine that we had with out lunch came from! So we had about 30 minutes to look around, take some pictures and buy some wine. After Casablanca we drove back to Santiago. Overall the tour was great! I loved the fact that it was I private tour, it was only my boyfriend and I and the van that Sean drove was very confortable!!! I really enjoyed the trip and really recommend it! Your guide did stop at the sand dunes in Concon and at a viewing point to watch the sea lions in Reñaca, which is a section of Viña del Mar. review_text: This is one of the three highlights of the Torres Del Paine national park - the others being the French Valley and Towers. These 3 highlights form the core of the W trek, which is how we visited it on our 1st day. There are a couple of other options for visiting the glacier - namely a boat ride (which I believe departs from the ferry terminal near Hotel Grey), kayaking or a minitrek on the ice. In this way it is similar to Perito Moreno in El Calafate - although the former is much larger and more impressive. For those on the W trek note that It has receded significantly in recent years. Although it once was in line with Refugio Grey it is now well back. You will begin to see it from afar at about the halfway mark on the 3.5 hour trail from Paine Grande to Refugio grey but for best views you need to walk around 1 hour north of refugio grey to the mirador. Note there is another mirador within 15 minutes but the one 1 hour north is the most impressive. It is located between the first and second suspension bridges and is clearly marked.

review_text: It is a small aquarium. I went with my 4-year-old son, who really likes fish. It has 3 floors, in which there are 4 aquariums (3 larger and 1 small), 3 pools with different species, and two rooms with fossils. We went on a Monday morning in January, and there was no one else waiting to enter. We had to wait for the guide (you cannot enter alone), the tour started at 10:30 and lasted approximately 25 minutes. The guide was very friendly, and explained each part of the aquarium to us. It has Chilean species in two large aquariums, and in the others there are fish from other places (Amazon and reefs). It's a nice place, but it's not big like Buin Zoo, so be careful with your expectations. It is for a small moment within the walk that can be touring the Prat pier.

review_text: My husband, daughter (11) and I spent four nights in TdP. The scenery is beyond spectacular, soaring mountains, thundering rivers, giant blue icebergs, enormous glaciers, wildlife galore, lakes in every shade of blue and green and unlimited options for adventure. The roads are very slow going and there are no gas stations-though we heard that the Serrano posada, near the Serrano ranger stations (where the helicopter is) may sell gas in 5 liter quantities. Be prepared for four seasons in one day-make sure you have rain/wind gear. Supplies are also very limited but available. This is a nature lover's paradise. The hike to the base of Las Torres while long (about 11.3 miles RT), while grueling, was beyond anything that I ever imagined. TdP is an absolute gem not to be missed.

review_text: El paseo dura alrededor de 1-1,5 hrs. Hay varias alternativas de botes que hacen el recorrido. Se puede pagar por arrendar el bote de manera individual o esperar que el bote se llene. Se recorren las cuevas, la catedra y la capilla. Todas estas son formaciones rocosas de mármol con unos colores increíbles. Si te toca sol, el paisaje en inigualable. Si toca viento podría ser complicado porque en la Patagonía el viento es realmente fuerte. He hecho el recorrido dos veces y en ambas me ha tocado sol y sin viento. No solo es lindo ver las formaciones rocosas, sino, también el lago color verde esmeralda y todo el entorno de cerros y glaciares que se alcanzan a ver. No es caro y si se pasa por el lugar (Puerto Tranquilo) es un panorama imperdible. The ride lasts about 1-1.5 hrs. There are several boat alternatives that make the journey. You can pay to rent the boat individually or wait for the boat to fill up. They go through the caves, the cathedral and the chapel. All these are marble rock formations with incredible colors. If you get sun, the landscape is second to none. If it touches wind it could be complicated because in the Patagonía the wind is really strong. I've done the tour twice and in both of them I've had sun and no wind. Not only is it nice to see the rock formations, but also the emerald green lake and the surrounding mountains and glaciers that can be seen. It is not expensive and if you pass by the place (Puerto Tranquilo) it is a must see.

review_text: I am an English-speaking business traveler and I had one day to tour Santiago during a business trip. I booked the "hop on, hop off" bus ticket so I could tour Santiago that day with a flexible schedule. I liked that the employees speak English, which is very helpful so I can ask questions and worry less about getting lost or having a problem, as a single, female traveler. I also liked the audio tour which you can choose in English or Spanish, and they provide ear buds for you, or you can use your own. This tour worked perfectly for me and I was glad that I used this option. My only recommendation is for Turistik to improve the visibility of their bus stops, which are not well marked, and sometimes I would "hop off" one place and need to "hop on" at another place. If only the company logo was placed high enough to see well at each bus stop, that would do the trip. Perhaps this is prohibited by the city of something because this seems like an obvious and easy improvement to make for tourists. Also, you can see a lot better from the top level of seats, so climb the stairs up to these seats if you are able to do so. Unlike the top "floor" of tour buses in some other cities, they do have rain protection on the top level. In Turistik we are very happy for your good experience with us and we hope to see you again in Santiago or that we have the opportunity of showing your friends around this part of Chile. review_text: Some personal notes before I begin, as you may find them useful. First, my husband has Parkinson's Disease, and therefore cannot walk too far or stand too long. Also, extreme heat is a problem, as is alcohol consumption. "Ah," you say, "but this is a Wine Tour." Not necessarily. Mauricio will tailor your tour to whatever activity levels and fields of interest that you request. We needed air conditioning and not much wine. He delivered. I can only try to speak to what other reviewers saw as shortcomings. While we considered it a terrific value, this is not a cheap tour. Those are easy to find through any Tourist Information Center. If that's what you are looking for, or you have the time and the fortitude to tackle a very large city on your own, then that’s what you should do. But time is money. For a truly special experience that will make the most of your time, and therefore your money, you have to trust the experience of a good guide and don't try to tell them their business. If this is you, please read on. We had only 3 nights and 2 days in Santiago and Valparaiso, and wanted to make the most of them. Mauricio was recommended to us by friends we trust, and he far exceeded our expectations. He was so exuberant that is was impossible not to be excited about what we were doing. Our flight arrived in the early evening, so when Mauricio picked us up at the airport, we only had time for a quick tour of town before hitting the hotel. We saw several areas of the city in twilight and dusk, and it was a wonderful way to be introduced to Santiago. Day two was a detailed tour of the city with visits to various districts and sites. This was followed by a journey into the countryside and a quick trip to a town that is known for its pottery. The place was very rustic and very interesting. If only we could have safely transported some of it! Lunch was typical Chilean food -- tastes we had never experienced and enjoyed very much. That evening he took us to a club for a folkloric performance. Now, we've all been to those (think Hawaiian Luau...), and the last thing we wanted was to be stuffed in a room with a bunch of tourists watching a tired old show. We were not. The majority of the clientele was local, celebrating birthdays or other special events. It was a slice of local color we would never have found on our own. The show was quite well done, with a sampling of songs and dances from the different cultural areas of Chile. But the best part of the evening for us was watching the locals dancing after the performers were finished. The uninhibited delight they took in moving to the music is something we won't soon forget. It was then we really knew we were in South America! The third day we breakfasted on Mauricio's favorite empanadas (amazing), on our way to a wine tasting (wonderful) and a museum. Foiled by a local strike of museum workers (what??), we headed out to the coast to a tiny -- no, VERY tiny -- fishing village for a fabulous fresher-than-fresh seafood lunch. Nothing like watching the boats containing dinner being brought in while you are eating the lunch they caught that morning. We continued on to Valparaiso and Concon where Mauricio and Ricardo (the terrific driver) dropped us at our hotel after a tour of the UNESCO Heritage Site. It was a stark contrast to the sophistication of Santiago, and very worth the trip. Lucky for us the site is a "living museum," as the strike was in force at all the indoor museums in town. There were lots of unhappy looking tourists wandering around while we saw what the city offered from the comfort of the van. In closing, I can only say if we had it to do over again, we would call Mauricio. If you are willing to put yourself in the hands of a guy who loves what he does, loves his country, and loves sharing it with others, you can't go wrong with Chilean Wine Lovers.

review_text: Date: February 1, 2009 Reviewer: kef252, Park City, Utah We discovered Mirador de Chepu quite serendipitously when other plans we’d had for Chiloe fell through. And are we ever glad they did! Our brief stay at this unique and beautiful refuge turned out to be the single best experience we had during our family’s 3-week travels throughout Chile. Owners, Fernando Claude and Amory Uslar, are trying to preserve a unique piece of sourthern Chile’s ecosystem by being completely self-sustaining, involving the locals, and promoting environmentally friendly tourism--and they are succeeding! The food, lodging & friendly interactions with our hosts could not have been better. Our 2 teenagers felt most welcomed and at home, especially enjoying the playful company of Luca, the family’s golden retriever puppy. Since we had only one day there, the hardest decision we had to make was whether to kayak on the mystical Chepu River at dawn or hike out to an isolated penguin colony. We chose the latter, and just before daybreak the next morning we embarked on a truly “other-worldy” adventure - an exhilirating boat ride and visually-stunning 2 -hour hike to a "hidden" island beach on the pacific coast that is home to a colony of Magellan and Humboldt penguins. This was no tourist destination! We were the only ones on the beach (with our very knowledgeable guide, Humberto) and right in the midst of the colony. We got as close as 5 or 6 feet to the very curious birds, who would cock their heads and glue their eyes on us, as fascinated with us as we were with them. Then, after several minutes of mutual admiration, something would spook them and off they would scurry down the rocks and into the water, only to return again minutes later for another look. This dance went on for an hour or so - we were enchanted indeed. Only the rising tide would force us to head home. Mirador de Chepu is truly an environmental paradise, made all the more special by the warmth and friendship of Fernando, Amory and Humberto. In truth, we would like to keep it a secret, all to ourselves for future visits, but that would be most unfair to all of you who have yet to experience this magical place – you will never forget it!

review_text: We ended up doing three tours with Turistik and it was a bit of a mixed bag. First of all the price... we started off thinking we'd been ripped off when we first shelled out for the tours, as they did seem really expensive. But having been in Santiago for five days now, I think it's more a case of Santiago / Chile being quite expensive generally, as relative to other things the tour prices kinda stack up. I think the deceptive thing when you're talking about a currency where you're paying tens of thousands is that you think things should therefore be cheap relative to the pound or the dollar, but that's not the case as things in chilean pesos cost a similar amount to back home. I guess the thing that did annoy us is, even after we got over the exchange rate, is that we were charged for our 3y/o son. Yes it was at a slightly discounted rate, but given that there was no food included on any tour, he wasn't in the least bit interested in any of the tours and he sat on our lap on the bus on each occasion (so wasn't taking up a space), it makes you wonder what he was paying for. That wasn't good. Better was the fact that Turistik did hotel pick-ups to take you to a central meeting point where the tours set off from. Not sure if that's a given when it comes to tours, but it saves you whatever transport cost to get to the departure point. In terms of the tours themselves, they were a bit mixed... The City Tour - I wouldn't bother given the chance again. I'd either go for the 'Hop on / Hop off' tour (same price, but much more flexibility to get off and see things and enjoy a sunny day if the weather's good), or just do it myself on the metro / by foot. The stops were fairly uninspiring i.e horse racing track and the central market Valparaiso / Vina del mar - this one I did think represented value for money. It's a full day and the two towns you visit are very nice in their own right. It's interesting and picturesque in equal measure and you stop at a really nice spot for lunch too (not included in price). Andes Panoramic - unspectacular. Perhaps it's dependent on the season and it's a better view when the snow's down. As it was, I didn't think the spot where this tour takes you was particularly great for photo opportunities. We also only stopped once, so were left to try and get pictures out of the window of the moving bus on the ascent, when there seemed to be better views at times Dear Samba2014 Thank you very much for your comments about our tours. We regret that your experience was not the best. We seek to satisfy our passengers, which is why for the safety of minors traveling with us, our policy is that all children over 2 years old must occupy a seat and therefore pay for this. On the tours you describe, we would like to mention that we must follow an itinerary and a specific schedule, this is why we do not make other stops. We assure you that the place we stop at Andes (Valle Nevado) offers the best view. We like you enjoyed our trip to Viña del Mar and Valparaíso, where we visit the best tourist attractions in the area; and that you consider a tour Hop On - Hop Off when you visit Santiago again!

review_text: We left the Pan American Highway and took a small country road to the valley which has great archaeological importance, being considered an open air museum of scientific and cultural interest. Groups of hunters inhabited the valley from around circa 2000 B.C. to A.D. 600. We were able to see incredible petroglyphs depicting masks, heads with antennae, tiara, sun symbols and snake and fish-like shapes deeply engraved in rocks on the hillside. Several pictographs of lineal drawings, human beings and other figures in natural paint were also visible. Numerous small cup stones or Piedras Tacitas were scattered throughout the area. The whole place has a sense of mystery and to date, no one has a clue what this was all about.

We spent about three and a half hours in the kitchen, chopping, preparing making pastry and then consuming a great meal, good wines and a Pisco Sour. Lots of fun, learnt something and did something different to the normal round of walking a city.

review_text: The Uncorked Wine Tour was easily the best experience during our week in Chile. Connie responded to our inquiry promptly and efficiently, noting that although the date we originally requested was already full, another day that week was available. We booked for this alternative date and were collected at our hotel at exactly the time agreed. We were told that one of the regular wineries was closed on this day but we didn't have to worry about this: Connie had already selected a replacement. On the drive it became clear that Connie was not only knowledgeable but relished any opportunity to discuss and educate. Each winery was interesting for different reasons: for instance, one employed biodynamic methods and while the architecture was very impressive, we also had a lively but friendly discussion about what a load of codswallop biodynamic - as explained to us by the winery's tour guide, at least - seemed to me to be. Other wineries included a magnificent veranda for a tasting and a tour of the vineyard itself. Lunch was unhurried and consisted of wine and food pairings in a very fine dining room. This afforded us an opportunity to get to know our fellow travellers a little more. Overall, a very nice day. The tour may not be not cheap if you've just spent some time in neighbouring Peru or Ecuador but it's nothing out of the ordinary for California or Europe and so it's a good price for a hassle-free day with a knowledgeable and enthusiastic tour guide which includes visits to at least three wineries and an extremely good lunch. Don't hesitate, just book! Review of: Best Wine Tasting in Santiago

review_text: We've down 4 to 9 day kayaking trips with companies from Alaska to Iceland to Thailand to NZ to Baja to Norway, and Kayak en Patagonia (& sister company Hello Patagonia) are as good as it gets. They are very safety conscious, with thorough instruction and superb gear from dry suits to boats (+tents/ bags if, as we did, you do their 3-day multi-day trip....for paddlers with some experience.) With >3 mile per hour river currents, covering 18 miles on the Rio Gray & 25 miles the next day on the Rio Serrano is no problem in the full-sized tandem sea kayaks which track and handle well Even in this often-windy environment, we didn't come close to capsizing or any other problems. Our guide Garrett was awesome, unflappable, with much knowledge, English & Spanish, great culinary skills, & a wonderfully calm, instructive manner. Highly respected company owner-operator Christian has a very professional operation on the rivers, and his wife Leslie (Hello Patagonia) can (and did) arrange in advance in a wonderfully helpful and thorough manner all sorts of other activities and logistics (refugios/ camps on the Torres del Paine "W" trek, bus & boat connections, hotels, glacier walks, etc.) She even co-led the eight-customer paddling day trip we joined (in English & Spanish) and is much fun, very informative. With safety and logistics "in hand" via Kayak en Patagonia, one can simply "sit back" and enjoy the Alaska-like world-class flatwater kayaking (snow-capped mountains, waterfalls, calving glaciers, National Parks, icebergs) here in one of Patagonia's best wilderness areas.

review_text: I was collected from my Hostal by Sebastian in a small van at 7:00am and then off to pick up the other people coming in this tour. I got to see a bit more of Santiago than I would have normally doing this. An hour from the city the air is so much clearer. I didn't realise how thick the air is there. We stopped at San Jose de Maipu for a walk through the Plaza with a tree talk. Our guide has a 'green' heart. He talked about reaforestation, trees on farms for windbreaks and fence lines.We saw kids o - cactus of the area. Rain sticks are made from these. We followed a dirt road and climbed up to 2500 metres above sea level. We passed what I thought was mass erosion of a hill but Sebastian said that it was actually a glacier that had made it this far, stopped then retreated. All that is left is dirt. We stopped a a quaint cafe with a toilet (flush!) a very long way from civilisation (don't forget to have coins/small change - public toilets require you to pay anything from 100 - 400 pesos for the privilege). Beautiful smell of woodsmoke and gorgeous snow views. We got to Embalse del Yeso the laguna then walked to the end of the road for more wonderful views of both the laguna and the mountains. Lunch was included : cheese, olives, almonds, peanuts, bread rolls with chicken tomato lettuce and mayo. 2 glasses of cab merlot and an apple to finish. Lovely to practise my español with other people on bus. Thanks a lot for your review! We give our best everyday to make the best experience for our tourists..so your comments makes us happy!

We had different guides and drivers on both trips, but they were all very punctual, friendly, knowledgable and helped to make both trips very unique. Whilst Valparaiso and Winery trip required little effort apart from a few hours walking, the Cajon Del Maipo Snow Shoe Trekking was a little more adventurous, but the views were worth the effort. review_text: Choosing the right tour for Uyuni may be a nightmare. Almost every agency in San Pedro is trying to convince you to go with them. And yes, Feel Atacama, is no different. But what made it different for us was how approachable the staff was and how far they are willing to go to accommodate to your wishes (without lies or promising things that won't happen). Feel Atacama works with Bolivian agency Uturunku that specialises in Uyuni tours. We took a 3 day tour with 2 night stay. Itinerary at first looked the same as others but there were three main differences: - Private bedroom on the first night (not a dorm) - Sunset at Uyuni on 2nd day (all other operators were insisting this is not possible) - Vegeterian food option without the need of promoting anyone to get it And other big advantage, the guide, Alfie!! Yes, he didn't speak English but god, he went miles to make our tour so so sooooo special. From extra view points, clear explanations of each stop, to great atmosphere in the car and smile all day long! We can't say a bad word about the organisation and we loved every second. We would like to thank Fran, Hans and especially Rodrigo from Feel Atacama for making our experience unforgettable.

review_text: My husband and I were lucky enough to stumble upon a Spicy Chile walking tour when we arrived early to our hostel in Santiago on our first day in the city. We had just arrived from the airport around 9 am, and had stored our bags in the hostel's storage closet, when our tour guide Nicholas walked in. He asked if anyone would be interested in a free walking tour, and we were on our way from there! We did "The Patrimonial Route", which took us through three neighborhoods - Concha y Toro, Brasil, and Yungay - and we saw buildings and sites that make up the varied history of Santiago and Chile itself. Other walking tours seem to take you to all the typical places (and are usually made up visits to statues, museums, and monuments), but Nicholas took us to the homes and haunts of famous (and not so famous) Santiago residents. We saw earthquake damage on historical buildings, restoration efforts, neighborhood gems, a barbershop that has been in business for over 150 years, several quirky restaurants, and learned the history behind a seemingly typical city plaza, as well as aspects of Chile's darker history. Nicholas was happy to answer any questions we had, and made sure he spoke equally to both the English-speaking and Spanish-speaking members of our group. We spent most of the morning and afternoon wandering the streets and lanes of these neighborhoods, and came out with an understanding of aspects of Santiago that you don't often find in travel guides. Thank you to Spicy Chile and Nicholas for helping us appreciate this city and spark a curiosity for it's history and residents :)

review_text: We spent two days in Pucon as we headed south through Chile, and luckily Sierra Nevada had two spots open on their Villarricca climb, and were able to get us on the hill the next day. This isn't a typical 'hike' as many travel books indicate. It requires cramp-ons, ice picks and various layers of insulated clothing, to be added as the altitude changes. Most of this was provided by Sierra Nevada; along with transportation to and from the volcano. We had 3 great guides who paced themselves with the varied speeds of the group. They were very knowledgable when determining which lines to take across the ice and snow, as well as avoiding some precarious looking rock formations. Some tips - bring lots of water (2L), and pack a lunch and snacks that will give you some sustained energy... you'll need it. This is a full day excursion. We would definitely book with Sierra Nevada again. A great company with friendly, professional staff.

review_text: As everyone should do when in South America, we did the three day trip from San Pedro to Uyuni. We (4 Dutch people) decided to go with World White Travel since they offered us an English guide with the driver. We had absolutely no regrets of this decision, which raised the price of the trip off course. We noticed that most drivers and guides usually work for more companies, so you will have to be a bit lucky about the people you get in wig, but our experience with The driver Richard and guide Juan were just awesome. The trips takes you through spectacular sights. First night was in a hostel, and was really cold. The lady that served us dinner was very friendly and they did the absolute best they could to make your stay as nice as possible. The hostels are basically a row of hostels, and are pretty much all the same for all agencies. Don't expect too much, then you'll be fine. It does get cold in the night though, so bring warm clothes. Personally I suffered from altitude sickness during the first night, since we slept at 4300m above sea level. Both the guide and our hostess were really kind serving me coca leaves and team which for me actually helped. During the second and third day you'll continue to Uyuni, visiting spectacular sites. Second night for us was also way better, being on a lower altitude, sleeping in a nicer hostel and having a hot shower, although her was just one. Overall, I'd recommend everyone to do this trip, don't expect too much of the accomodations, and just be impressed by the amazing views and drive that will stay with you for the rest of your life.

review_text: The Metro in Valparaiso – Vina Del Mar area runs from the port area at Valparaiso adjacent to the main Square Plaza Sotomayor along the coastline and then underground through Vina del Mar and eastwards to major shopping centres. It is a single line and very new. The train runs on rubber tyres and is much quieter than the Metro in Santiago. The disadvantage of the Valparaiso Metro is that it only runs about every 20 minutes each way. And it is not as crowded as the Santiago Metro. The cost is dependent on the distance (unlike Santiago) but the journey from Puerto to our station in Vina Del Mar was 400 pesos each way – cheaper than Santiago Metro. You have to purchase a card to use the system and then buy credit to put on the card to cover the journeys. You need to both swipe on when beginning a journey and swipe off at the end of your journey. The Metro worked very well for us as taxies in Valparaiso are much more expensive than in Santiago and we felt that we saved money by staying in a better and lower cost hotel in Vina del Mar and commuting with a 15 minute Metro Journey rather than staying on the hills above Valparaiso and paying the cost of a taxi – at least for the uphill section!! The Metro in Valparaiso – Vina del Mar is clean, convenient and fast and we would recommend other travellers make use of it also.

review_text: Christopher and his friendly associates run a cozy boutique wine shop on one of Santiago's hippest streets. This is a great place to stop for a lively chat and perhaps a taste break while out and about in Barrio Italia. For such a tiny shop, they offer an exceptional selection from small scale Chilean wineries, with many wines that are unavailable at larger chain stores or on supermarket shelves. Be aware that "boutique" here does not mean everything is priced for wealthy drinkers. There are fine bottles in the 8,000 - 12,000 peso range, including even rare varietals (in Chile anyway) like Albariño and Petit Sirah. I also love their tasting events, typically on a Saturday or Sunday afternoon, when producers present and pour their wines in the sunny, comfortable mezzanine restaurant area. The only negative is a dispute with the restaurant downstairs about opening bottles bought at La Cava to accompany a meal. I hope by now they could settle on the corking fee or otherwise make a deal that benefits both businesses. La Cava del Barrio offers something for every taste and price point. Winos will certainly be intrigued by what they discover here!

review_text: Due to the wind our kayak experience was cancelled after 10mins from launching. We made it barely 100m from the launch site, at which point the experienced guide almost capsized his kayak and we began a hasty retreat back to shore, with the guides putting in place a safety “boat” type manoeuvre tying the kayaks together. We got closer to the glacier ice the previous day on the footpath! The guide admitted that we shouldn’t have gone out in those conditions. We understand we could not proceed further due to wind conditions but this could have been pre-empted (the weather was poor and all kayak tours were cancelled the previous day). It felt like the team simply put us out at risk so they could charge us the fees rather than cancelling the experience for the second day in a row and refunding the group. We would expect that Bigfoot should have some sort of partial refund process for this type of scenario for a tour that is sold as a 3hr experience but then only lasted 1hour, with only 10mins on the lake in kayaks. We understand that Bigfoot incurred some costs in this short ride and that they may have started the trip in good faith but given the early cancellation, charging the whole price feels like being ripped off sadly. The staff simply shrugged and said it’s in the small print. This risk should be much much more clearly flagged to people when booking if this is the policy, given the nature of the winds in Patagonia and the high likelihood of this happening to most trips. Staff were all friendly and the equipment good quality, but the above left a sour taste in the mouth. Profit above safety and customer experience is not a good look.

review_text: Our next stop was Pablo Neruda’s house, La Chascona. Neruda was the second Chilean poet to be awarded the Nobel Prize for Literature, in 1971. The first Chilean poet to be awarded the prize was Gabriela Mistral, in 1945. While Neruda’s father opposed his son’s interest in writing, Neruda received encouragement from many others including Gabriela Mistral who was the principle at the local girls’ school. He led a fascinating dual life as a poet and diplomat. La Chascona is one of his three houses in Chile, all of which are now part of the Foundation Pablo Neruda and open to the public. It was built in 1953 to house his then mistress, Matilde Urrutia. He called the house La Chascona in her honour as that was the nickname he had given her due to her abundant red hair. The house is a series of small buildings and rooms at the edge of the city, most of which Neruda designed himself over a period of five years. One architect who worked with him on the house commented that on one occasion Neruda had a window, armchair and painting that were favourites and he created a corner space in which to enclose them, conditioning the space to the object (rather than the conventional manner of placing the objects in the space). Another architect observed that Neruda modelled his spaces in the interest of the ‘intimacy of the interior ambient’. The dining table, for instance, is long and very narrow in order to ‘keep his guests close together’. Walking around the house you get a sense of a very warm and comfortable and personal living space. Neruda was a great collector of knick knacks and kitsch and the house is filled but not overcrowded with these items that he collected on his travels around the world. (No photos allowed)

review_text: Our experience with Sorbac was AMAZING. With Sorbac, you never feel like you are touring with an agency - we felt like we were visiting friends who were showing us around, a feeling I have never had in any other place. With only 4 days to enjoy Atacama, we couldn’t have hoped for a better way to make use of every minute. From the moment we arrived, the boys made sure to adapt everything possible to best fit our schedule and interests. You always feel like you are a priority and they really make you feel like your trip, at that moment, is the most important thing. They are extremely transparent and flexible with you at all times. You can really tell they are an honest group of friends who love what they do and love sharing experiences with those who visit. The tours are a step ahead of the agencies in San Pedro - and you don’t have to tour with the other agencies to figure that out (we didn’t). The tours are fun, relaxed, the boys are incredibly patient, the food served during the tours is DELICIOUS, the setting of the table during meals is straight out of a catalogue and they take you to places that other agencies don’t, so you end up in situations where you are completely alone in the middle of nowhere. We had 3 nights, so we stayed 2 nights at Casa Sorbac and 1 night camping. I strongly recommend doing the camping night - the scenery is beautiful, the boys make sure everything you need is taken care of and you get to enjoy a night of stargazing, listening to music, dancing, eating and chilling with a super fun group of friends - at no point do you feel like they are anything but your friends. We ended our short stay anxious to go back - which we surely will - and with great new friends who we couldn’t thank enough for being so incredible to us.

review_text: We drove to the village of Punta de Choros, which is the where the trip to the islands begin. It costs about US$16.00 per person for the boat trip plus US $4.00 per person for entrance to the national park. When we arrived the wind was starting to blow hard and we were the last boat out so the ride was a little rough to the islands. It takes about 30 to 40 minutes to get to the islands but it was worth it. The sea lions, the bird life and penguins abounded. Unfortunately due to the weather the dolphins were not about. Apparently according to the local fishermen, the best time to see them , and the swim alongside the boats, is early , when the weather is quiet and you're on the last boat out. A great trip to make, but do check the weather forecast for the day in detail. It can get quite choppy and the Navy personnel there will not allow any boats to leave. Most boats are small and so if your're afraid of boats I wouldn't advice it.

review_text: I did 2 others trip with Ecochile adventure, and it was much better than expected. After my first short bike trip, it was easier to plan something different and to plan something that would better fill my dream. So they took me to El Morado, but in the next valley where lanscape is better and where there is less walking. This has been the option choosen because of the time I had left in Santiago (flight at 19h). I got pick up at 7h in the morning and they have used a car that can go very high in the mountain. The trip was amazing, we saw also some ice falling from the glacier. When I finished my job in Chile, I contacted them again since I had some free time before my flight back to Canada. We stayed close to Santiago and did a 800m elevation gain to a nice summit. They choose again something not usual that was perfect for me. This time more hicking and a summit where we could see the Andes and the Santiago smog. We were lucky because it was very claudy in Santiago and we hicked high enough to get above the clouds. Amazing! Thanks to Cristian for the planning and good communication and also to Joaquin the guide that choose the perfect trip for me and to be so friendly and so easy to deal with. After 3 trips, its like a friend that I will sure contact again if I come back.
